body.statement: Let \(0<p_0\le1\), \(0<v_0\le q_L<q_H\le1\), \(e_0\le1/2\), \(\rho_0\le1/4\), and \(0<\mu_n\le1\). Then \(P_n^A,P_n^B\in\mathcal M_{4n}\). They have the same \(N=4n\), \(K=4\), target composition, aggregate compliance \(\mu_D=\mu_n\), source sample sizes, source cell masses, propensities, and labeled multiset of per-source prices \(\{q_L,q_L,q_H,q_H\}\), and neither collection contains a source covering both target cells. Nevertheless, \[V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P_n^A,0)=\frac{q_L+q_H}{8n}>\frac{q_Lq_H}{2n(q_L+q_H)}=V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P_n^B,0),\qquad V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P_n^A,0)-V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P_n^B,0)=\frac{(q_H-q_L)^2}{8n(q_L+q_H)}.\] Therefore their exact pooled observed-data information bounds \(1/V_{\mathrm{coll}}\), their collection strengths, and their strong-branch honest-length benchmarks are strictly different. No scalar single-source or Kish-style reduction based on pooled size, aggregate compliance, target composition, and marginal per-source precision summaries can represent both collections while retaining observed support; the joint incidence of precision and cell support is necessary.
body.justification: This strict-separation corollary of the pooled-information equivalence is non-definitional: the source-by-cell precision incidence, rather than a pooled effective sample size, controls inference.
body.gap: Published multi-source efficiency formulas do not exhibit two collection-only encouragement designs matched on scalar summaries but separated by the support-constrained residual program.
body.consumer: Trial portfolio design must match precise sources to target cells rather than report only total enrollment or a Kish effective size.
